title: What is known about 1RB---_1RC0RA_1LD0RB_0LE0LC_1RE1LF_0RD0RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_1RC0RA_1LD0RB_0LE0LC_1RE1LF_0RD0RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of blocks (01)^n separated by single 0s, with a few markers (00, 10, 110). The head sweeps over the list and the right end grows by about one block per sweep; markers travel through the list, each passage changing the lengths of the blocks it crosses by small amounts (±1, ±2 early on, ±15, ±30, ±90 later), while the blocks at the other end freeze. It is the mirror image of 1RB0LE_0RC0RA_1LC1RD_0LB0LE_1LA0LF_1LE--- with another start state. The shift rules over the background are proved in Lean; no macro map is known yet.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 139,537 cells have been visited and 69,737 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.095). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.517).

claims.title: Shift rules over the (01) background
claims.text: How the head crosses (01)^n and (10)^n in each direction, for every n (2n steps each).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: A plain C simulator (longrun.c, on tools/c/tm.h) runs 1011 steps from blank tape without a halt; at the end the head has visited cells -296 to 856,865 and 428,540 cells hold a 1.

claims.title: Same rule table as 1RB0LE_0RC0RA_1LC1RD_0LB0LE_1LA0LF_1LE---
claims.text: Reflecting the tape and renaming the states turns this machine into 1RB0LE_0RC0RA_1LC1RD_0LB0LE_1LA0LF_1LE---; this machine starts in the state that corresponds to F there. The two runs from blank tape are different orbits of the same rule table (they do not meet in the first 2·104 steps), with the same kind of behaviour.

claims.title: Frozen list, active front
claims.text: In the defect picture the walls far from the growing end stop moving while new ones are born at that end and slow down as they move inward. This is the shape of a counter-like process, with no visible drift toward a halting configuration.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The marker dynamics on the list has not been reduced to a map.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine keeps a list of blocks of 01s that grows at the right end; little markers travel through the list and nudge the block lengths, and the far end of the list freezes.

facts.text: How the head crosses the (01) background, proved for every length.
No halt in the C simulator.

sections.heading: Markers running through a list
html: Read at the moments the head reaches the growing end, the tape is (01)^n1 0 (01)^n2 0 … with a handful of markers in place of some single 0s. The head crosses each block in two steps per copy (proved), and at a marker it turns or changes phase; each sweep moves markers by a block or so and changes the lengths of the blocks around them.

Early on (up to about 2·106 steps) the blocks change by −1, +2, −2, +2 on alternate passes, and all signs flip when the first block is absorbed at the end wall. Later a zone of active markers changes blocks by multiples of 15 while the rest of the list stays frozen. How these signals are generated and what they compute is the next thing to work out.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.095). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.517).
After 109 steps the tape spans 139,537 cells (140 left of the start, 80,706 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: Signals on a list of (01)^n blocks: markers 0, 00, 10, 110 travel through the list and shift block lengths (mirror pair)
summary: A list of (01)^n blocks separated by single 0s grows at the right end; markers (00, 10, 110) run through the list and move copies between neighbouring blocks, while the far part of the list freezes; the mirror image of 1RB0LE_0RC0RA_1LC1RD_0LB0LE_1LA0LF_1LE--- up to the start state.
